questions.question: In March 2025, the Disaster Management (Amendment) Bill 2024 was passed in the Lok Sabha. This bill seeks to amend which of the following Acts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Disaster Management Act, 2005**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Disaster Management (Amendment) Bill, 2024** was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** on **August 1, 2024**, and subsequently passed in **March 2025** to amend the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**.
 
• The primary objective of the amendment is to bring more **clarity and convergence** in the roles of various authorities working in the field of disaster management at the **National** and **State** levels.
 
• One of the significant features of the Bill is the establishment of a **National Disaster Database**, which will be maintained at the national level to store critical information related to disaster risks and mitigation.
 
• The Bill provides for the constitution of **Urban Disaster Management Authorities** in state capitals and large cities with **Municipal Corporations**, acknowledging the unique challenges of urban flooding and infrastructure risks.
 
• It grants **statutory recognition** to existing bodies such as the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** and the **State Disaster Response Force (SDRF)**, formalizing their roles and responsibilities within the legal framework.
 
• The amendment empowers the **Central Government** to make regulations concerning the **Disaster Management** framework, ensuring a more flexible and responsive system to modern-day calamities. ***Hence, the correct answer is The Disaster Management Act, 2005.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Disaster Management Act, 2005**:
 
 
• This Act was enacted by the **Parliament of India** on **December 23, 2005**, following the devastating **2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami**.
 
• It established a three-tier structure: the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** at the center, the **State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA)** at the state level, and the **District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA)** at the district level.
 
• The **Prime Minister of India** serves as the ex-officio **Chairperson** of the **NDMA**, while the **Chief Ministers** lead the respective **SDMAs**.
 
 
 
• **Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897**:
 
 
• This is a colonial-era law meant to provide for the better prevention of the spread of dangerous epidemic diseases. It was widely invoked during the **COVID-19 pandemic** in **2020**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Protection Act, 1986**:
 
 
• Enacted in the wake of the **Bhopal Gas Tragedy**, this Act empowers the **Central Government** to protect and improve environmental quality and control pollution.
 
 
 
• **National Green Tribunal Act, 2010**:
 
 
• This Act enabled the creation of the **National Green Tribunal (NGT)** for the effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to **environmental protection** and conservation of forests.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Revisions in 2024 Bill**:
 
 
• The **2024 Bill** seeks to address the "overlapping" of functions between the **NDMA** and various ministries, ensuring that the **National Plan** is more comprehensive.
 
• It introduces provisions for **financial penalties** for individuals or organizations that fail to comply with the directions issued by the **Central** or **State Governments** regarding disaster management.
 
• The creation of the **National Disaster Database** is expected to help in **evidence-based decision-making** by tracking the **allocation and utilization** of funds from the **National Disaster Response Fund**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following districts emerged as the best-performing district in the Northeastern Region according to the 2023–24 SDG Index released by NITI Aayog in July 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hnahthial (Mizoram)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **NER District SDG Index 2023–24**, which is the **second edition** of the index released by **NITI Aayog**, **Hnahthial** district in **Mizoram** secured the **first rank** in the **Northeastern Region**.
 
• **Hnahthial** achieved a top score of **75.39** out of **100**, indicating significant progress across various socio-economic and environmental parameters.
 
• The index was developed by **NITI Aayog** in collaboration with the **Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER)** and with technical support from the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**.
 
• Following **Hnahthial**, the district of **Aizawl** in **Mizoram** stood **second** with a score of **75.24**, while **Siaha** (also in **Mizoram**) and **East Sikkim** (Sikkim) followed closely in the rankings.
 
• The **2023–24** edition of the index evaluated the performance of **103 districts** across the **eight states** of Northeast India using a framework of **84 indicators** spanning **15 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Hnahthial (Mizoram).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**

 
 
• The **SDGs** are a collection of **17 global goals** set by the **United Nations** in **2015** to be achieved by the **year 2030**. They cover issues like **poverty, hunger, health, education, climate change, and social justice**.
 
• In India, **NITI Aayog** is the nodal agency responsible for monitoring the progress of these goals at the **national and sub-national levels**.
 
 
 
• **NER District SDG Index:**
 
 
• This regional index is specifically designed to address the **unique challenges** and **geographical diversity** of the **North Eastern Region**, ensuring that development is tailored to local needs.
 
• The **eight states** covered are **Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura**.
 
 
 
• **Performance Categorization:**
 
 
• Districts are categorized based on their **SDG scores**: **Aspirant (0–49)**, **Performer (50–64)**, **Front Runner (65–99)**, and **Achiever (100)**.
 
• In the latest report, **all 103 districts** in the **NER** fell into either the **Front Runner** or **Performer** categories, showing a general upward trend in development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India):**

 
 
• It was established on **1 January 2015**, replacing the **Planning Commission**. It functions as the **premier policy think tank** of the **Government of India**.
 
• The **Prime Minister** serves as the **Ex-officio Chairperson**, while the **Vice-Chairperson** and **CEO** lead the administrative functions.
 
 
 
• **SDG India Index 2023–24 (National Level):**
 
 
• At the **national level**, the **SDG India Index 2023–24** showed that **Uttarakhand** and **Kerala** were the **top-performing states**, while **Bihar** was ranked at the bottom.
 
• The **national composite score** for India improved from **66 in 2020-21** to **71 in 2023-24**, reflecting significant advancements in **Goal 1 (No Poverty)** and **Goal 13 (Climate Action)**.
 
 
 
• **Goal-Specific Performance in NER:**
 
 
• **Mizoram** and **Sikkim** have consistently performed well in **Goal 3 (Good Health and Well-being)** and **Goal 4 (Quality Education)**, contributing to the high ranking of their districts like **Hnahthial** and **Aizawl**.

questions.question: On 1 September 2025, the rupee ___________ to a record low before recovering after likely RBI intervention.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fell to ₹88.33 per USD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **1 September 2025**, the **Indian Rupee** experienced significant selling pressure, causing it to breach a new historic low of **₹88.33** against the **US Dollar**.
 
• The primary drivers for this depreciation included a strengthening **US Dollar Index (DXY)** and consistent **Foreign Institutional Investor (FII)** outflows from the **Indian capital markets**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the fall to 88.33 is correct.***
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** reportedly intervened in the **Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF)** and spot markets by selling **US Dollars** through **public sector banks** to provide support to the local currency.
 
• Global economic factors, such as high **crude oil prices** and rising **US Treasury yields**, contributed to the rupee's vulnerability, as India is a major importer of energy.
 
• The intervention by the central bank was aimed at curbing **excessive volatility** rather than targeting a specific exchange rate level, allowing the rupee to recover slightly after hitting the record low.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Currency Depreciation:**
 
 
• This is the fall in the value of a currency in a **floating exchange rate system** due to market forces like **demand and supply**.
 
• A weaker rupee makes **exports more competitive** but increases the cost of **imports**, leading to **imported inflation** in the domestic economy.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**
 
 
• The **RBI** manages the exchange rate through its **Foreign Exchange Reserves**, which include **Foreign Currency Assets (FCA)**, **Gold**, **Special Drawing Rights (SDRs)**, and the **Reserve Position in the IMF**.
 
• In **2024-2025**, India’s **Forex Reserves** have been maintained at high levels to shield the economy from **external shocks** and speculative attacks on the currency.
 
 
 
• **External Factors:**
 
 
• The **monetary policy** of the **US Federal Reserve** plays a crucial role; when the **Fed** raises interest rates, capital often flows back to the **United States**, weakening currencies in **Emerging Markets** like **India**.
 
• The **Current Account Deficit (CAD)** is also a vital indicator; a widening deficit puts structural pressure on the **rupee's value** over the long term.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Exchange Rate Management:** Unlike a fixed regime, India follows a **managed float** system where the market determines the rate, but the **RBI** steps in to prevent **wild fluctuations**.
 
• **Impact on Sectors:**
 
 
• **Beneficiaries:** **IT services**, **textiles**, and **pharmaceuticals** often benefit from a weaker rupee as their **dollar-denominated earnings** translate into more rupees.
 
• **Losers:** **Oil marketing companies**, **importers of electronics**, and **students studying abroad** face higher costs when the rupee falls to record lows like **88.33**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:** The rupee has seen a gradual depreciation over the decades, moving from around **₹4.76** in **1947** to over **₹80** in **2022**, and reaching the **₹88** mark in late **2025**.

3f:T24b1,

questions.question: On 26 May 2025, which government agency released a report titled 'Designing a Policy for Medium Enterprises', offering a comprehensive roadmap for transforming medium enterprises into future growth engines of India’s economy?

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **26 May 2025**, the **NITI Aayog** released a landmark report titled **'Designing a Policy for Medium Enterprises'**, which outlines a strategic framework to bolster the growth of the **MSME** sector. ***Hence, the correct answer is NITI Aayog.***
 
• The report identifies **Medium Enterprises** as the "missing middle" in India's industrial landscape and proposes a dedicated roadmap to transform them into globally competitive **growth engines**.
 
• Key recommendations in the report focus on **Ease of Doing Business (EoDB)**, providing better **access to credit**, and facilitating **technological upgrades** for firms that have graduated from being small-scale units.
 
• The document emphasizes the need for **structural reforms** to help these enterprises integrate into **Global Value Chains (GVCs)**, thereby contributing significantly to India's goal of becoming a **USD 5 trillion economy**.
 
• It suggests the creation of **sector-specific clusters** and specialized **Export Promotion Cells** to assist **Medium Enterprises** in expanding their footprint in international markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Medium Enterprises:**
 
 
• According to the revised **MSME classification** effective from **1 July 2020**, an enterprise is categorized as **Medium** if its investment in plant and machinery or equipment does not exceed **Rs. 50 crore** and its annual turnover does not exceed **Rs. 250 crore**.
 
• This composite criteria of **investment and turnover** was introduced to encourage firms to scale up without fear of losing **government benefits**.
 
 
 
• **About NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• The **National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog)** was established on **1 January 2015**, replacing the erstwhile **Planning Commission**.
 
• It serves as the apex **public policy think tank** of the **Government of India**, providing both directional and policy inputs while fostering **Cooperative Federalism**.
 
• The **Prime Minister of India** acts as the ex-officio **Chairperson** of the Aayog.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the MSME Sector:**
 
 
• The **Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME)** sector is often called the **backbone of the Indian economy**, contributing nearly **30%** to the **GDP** and approximately **45%** to total **exports**.
 
• It provides employment to over **11 crore people** across the country, making it the second-largest employer after **agriculture**.
 
• Schemes like **Udyam Registration**, the **RAMP (Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance)** program, and the **Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS)** are designed to support this vital sector.
 
 
 
• **Role of Other Agencies:**
 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** regulates the flow of **Priority Sector Lending (PSL)** to MSMEs.
 
• The **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** facilitates capital raising for smaller firms through **SME Exchanges** like **NSE Emerge** and **BSE SME**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: In 2025, Uttar Pradesh and which other state hosted the Defence Industrial Corridor that together have attracted investments worth over ₹8,658 crore?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Government of India has established two **Defence Industrial Corridors (DICs)** in the country, one in **Uttar Pradesh** and the other in **Tamil Nadu**, to promote self-reliance in defence manufacturing.
 
• As of the recent updates leading into **2024-2025**, these two corridors have successfully attracted cumulative investments worth over **₹8,658 crore**, demonstrating a significant push toward **indigenous production**.
 
• The **Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridor (TNDIC)** consists of five strategic nodes: **Chennai**, **Hosur**, **Salem**, **Coimbatore**, and **Tiruchirappalli**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the second state is correct.***
 
• The **Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor (UPDIC)** is spread across six nodes: **Agra**, **Aligarh**, **Chitrakoot**, **Jhansi**, **Kanpur**, and **Lucknow**.
 
• The primary objective of these corridors is to create a robust **ecosystem** for defence production, involving both **Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs)** and **private sector** players, including **MSMEs** and **Startups**.
 
• These corridors were announced in the **Union Budget 2018-19** to reduce the **import dependency** of the Indian Armed Forces and bolster the **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** initiative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridor (TNDIC):**
 
 
• The state of **Tamil Nadu** was selected due to its existing strong **manufacturing base** and high rank in the **Export Preparedness Index**.
 
• The **Tiruchirappalli** node focuses heavily on **ordnance factories**, while **Chennai** leverages its **port accessibility** for global supply chains.
 
• Major companies like **Tata Group**, **L&T**, and **TVS** have expressed significant investment interests in this corridor.
 
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor (UPDIC):**
 
 
• The **Lucknow** node is being developed as a hub for **aerospace** and **missile technology**, including projects like the **BrahMos** missile unit.
 
• The **Aligarh** node has seen rapid development with several **small-scale industries** setting up units for components and hardware.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Defence Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **Department of Defence Production** facilitates these corridors by providing **infrastructure support** and testing facilities.
 
• The **Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX)** scheme is integrated with these corridors to foster **innovation** and technology development by **Startups**.
 
• The government has implemented the **Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP) 2020**, which prioritizes **Buy (Indian-IDDM)** categories to support local industries.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• The corridors are expected to generate massive **employment opportunities** (direct and indirect) for skilled youth in **North and South India**.
 
• By the year **2025**, the government aims to achieve a **turnover of ₹1,75,000 crore** (US$ 25 billion) in defence manufacturing, including **exports of ₹35,000 crore**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The investment of **₹8,658 crore** is a combined figure reflecting the progress made in both states since the inception of the project.
 
• The **Defence Investor Cell** has been created within the **Ministry of Defence** to provide **single-window clearance** and assistance to potential investors in these corridors.
 
• A total of **108 Positive Indigenisation Lists** have been notified by the government, ensuring that the items listed are sourced only from **domestic manufacturers** located within such industrial hubs.

questions.question: The 6th edition of the UMAI National Muaythai Championship was held in June 2025. What was its host city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rohtak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **6th edition** of the **UMAI National Muaythai Championship** was successfully organized in the city of **Rohtak**, located in the state of **Haryana**.
 
• Scheduled and held in **June 2025**, the championship saw participation from hundreds of athletes representing various states and Union Territories across **India**.
 
• The event was conducted under the aegis of the **United Muaythai Association - India (UMAI)**, which is the national governing body for the sport, affiliated with the **International Federation of Muaythai Associations (IFMA)**.
 
• The primary objective of holding the championship in **Rohtak** was to provide a professional platform for **Muaythai** practitioners to showcase their skills and to select the national team for upcoming **international tournaments**.
 
• The city of **Rohtak** was chosen due to its robust **sports infrastructure** and its reputation as a hub for **combat sports** in **North India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding Muaythai:**
 
 
• Known as the **"Art of Eight Limbs,"** **Muaythai** is a traditional martial art from **Thailand** that utilizes **fists**, **elbows**, **knees**, and **shins** for striking.
 
• It was officially recognized by the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** during the **138th IOC Session** held in **Tokyo** in **July 2021**, making it eligible for future **Olympic Games**.
 
 
 
• **United Muaythai Association - India (UMAI):**
 
 
• **UMAI** is responsible for the **development**, **regulation**, and **promotion** of **Muaythai** throughout the **Republic of India**.
 
• It ensures that Indian athletes adhere to the **anti-doping regulations** set by the **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)** and the **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA)**.
 
 
 
• **Rohtak as a Sports Destination:**
 
 
• **Rohtak** is home to the **Rajiv Gandhi Sports Complex**, which features world-class facilities for various indoor and outdoor sports.
 
• The state of **Haryana** has a long-standing history of producing **medal-winning athletes** in **wrestling**, **boxing**, and now **Muaythai**, contributing significantly to India's tally in the **Asian Games** and **Commonwealth Games**.
 
 
 
• **Championship Categories:**
 
 
• The **National Muaythai Championship** typically features weight categories ranging from **45 kg** to over **91 kg** for **male** and **female** participants.
 
• Divisions include **Elite Senior**, **Under-23**, and **Youth** categories (Junior and Sub-Junior), ensuring a pipeline of talent for the **national squad**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **2025 championship** in **Rohtak** served as a crucial **qualification event** for the **IFMA World Muaythai Championships**.
 
• The event highlighted the growing popularity of **martial arts** in **India**, with an increasing number of **female athletes** participating in **full-contact combat sports**.
 
• State governments, particularly **Haryana**, have been incentivizing such national championships to promote **sports tourism** and **youth engagement**.
</ul

questions.question: Which among the following technology-based methods of beneficiary registration under Poshan 2.0 was announced for implementation from 1st August 2025 during the Zonal Meeting at Kevadia, Gujarat, organised by the Ministry of Women and Child Development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Biometric Authentication System**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD)** announced the mandatory implementation of the **Biometric Authentication System** for beneficiary registration under **Poshan 2.0**, effective from **1st August 2025**.
 
• This significant decision was communicated during the **Zonal Meeting** held at **Kevadia, Gujarat** (near the Statue of Unity), where representatives from various states and Union Territories gathered to review the progress of nutrition and women empowerment schemes.
 
• The introduction of **biometric-based verification** aims to enhance transparency and ensure that the benefits of **Take Home Ration (THR)** and **Hot Cooked Meals (HCM)** reach the intended **genuine beneficiaries** without leakages.
 
• The system will involve **Aadhaar-based authentication** or other biometric markers to verify the physical presence of **children (0-6 years)**, **pregnant women**, and **lactating mothers** at **Anganwadi Centres (AWCs)**.
 
• By transitioning to this technology-based method, the government intends to eliminate **"ghost beneficiaries"** and streamline the data recorded on the **Poshan Tracker** application. ***Hence, the correct answer is Biometric Authentication System.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0:**
 
 
• Launched in **2021-22**, it is an **Integrated Nutrition Support Programme** that seeks to address the challenges of **malnutrition** in children, adolescent girls, pregnant women, and lactating mothers.
 
• The mission focuses on **three primary verticals**: Nutrition Support for **POSHAN**, Early Childhood Care and Education (**ECCE**), and **Anganwadi Infrastructure**.
 
• It targets the reduction of **Stunting**, **Under-nutrition**, **Anemia**, and **Low Birth Weight** across the country.
 
 
 
• **Poshan Tracker Application:**
 
 
• It is a robust **ICT-based platform** launched by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development** for **real-time monitoring** of nutrition service delivery.
 
• The application enables **Anganwadi Workers (AWWs)** to enter data regarding **growth monitoring**, **vaccination**, and **ration distribution**.
 
• As of recent data, more than **10 crore beneficiaries** are registered on the platform, and it tracks the **Height and Weight** of children monthly to identify **Wasting** and **Stunting**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Administrative Strategy:** The shift to **Biometric Authentication** is a part of the government's **Digital India** initiative to improve **governance** and **accountability** in social welfare programs.
 
• **Geographic Focus:** The choice of **Kevadia, Gujarat** for the **Zonal Meeting** highlights the focus on sharing **best practices** and regional cooperation among **Western States** and **UTs**.
 
• **Infrastructure Upgrade:** Under the **Saksham Anganwadi** component, over **2 lakh Anganwadis** are being upgraded with better **connectivity**, **clean water**, and **digital learning tools** to support the new authentication protocols.

questions.question: The new FASTag Annual plan system is specifically NOT designed for which type of vehicles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Commercial trucks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **FASTag Annual Plan** or **Monthly Pass** system is a specialized subscription model designed primarily for **private vehicle** owners who reside within a specific proximity of a **toll plaza**.
 
• **Commercial trucks** are classified as **Heavy Goods Vehicles (HGV)** or **Multi-Axle Vehicles (MAV)** and are typically excluded from these specific personal annual plans, as they are governed by **commercial tolling rates** based on load and distance. ***Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.***
 
• Vehicles like **Private cars**, **Jeeps**, and **Vans** are categorized under **Class 4** (Light Motor Vehicles) and are the primary beneficiaries of discounted passes if they are used for **non-commercial** purposes. ***Hence, options 2, 3, and 4 are incorrect as they are included in such plans.***
 
• The **National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)** implemented these plans to provide relief to local residents, allowing for unlimited trips within a **calendar month** or year for a fixed nominal fee, provided the vehicle is registered for **personal use**.
 
• The eligibility for these annual or monthly plans often requires the vehicle owner to provide **proof of residence** within a **20-kilometer radius** of the specific toll plaza where the plan is to be applied.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **FASTag Technology:**
 
 
• It utilizes **Radio Frequency Identification (RFID)** technology for making toll payments directly from the linked prepaid or savings account.
 
• The **FASTag** is affixed on the **windscreen** of the vehicle and enables a person to drive through toll plazas without stopping for **cash transactions**.
 
• As of **February 15, 2021**, the **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways** made **FASTag** mandatory for all vehicles in India to ensure seamless traffic flow and reduce **fuel consumption**.
 
 
 
• **Vehicle Classification and Toll Fees:**
 
 
• Vehicles are divided into classes such as **Class 4 (Cars/Jeeps/Vans)**, **Class 5 (Light Commercial Vehicles)**, **Class 6 (Bus/Truck)**, and **Class 7 (MAV)**.
 
• **Commercial trucks** often pay significantly higher toll rates than private vehicles because of the higher **wear and tear** they cause to the **highway infrastructure**.
 
• The **National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) Rules, 2008**, govern the structure of these fees and the provision of **monthly passes** for local traffic.
 
 
 
• **One Vehicle, One FASTag Initiative:**
 
 
• Launched by **NHAI** in **2024**, this initiative aims to discourage the use of a single **FASTag** for multiple vehicles or linking multiple **FASTags** to a single vehicle.
 
• It enhances the efficiency of **Electronic Toll Collection (ETC)** and ensures that the vehicle class registered matches the physical vehicle passing through the **toll lane**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **IHMCL (Indian Highway Management Company Limited):** This organization, incorporated by **NHAI**, carries out **Electronic Tolling** and other ancillary projects of **National Highways**.
 
• **Issuing Entities:** **FASTags** are issued by over **30 certified banks** and various **Point of Sale (POS)** locations across the country, including **petrol pumps** and **Common Service Centres (CSC)**.
 
• **Validity:** A **FASTag** typically has a validity of **5 years**, but the linked **annual plans** or **monthly passes** must be renewed periodically as per the **NHAI guidelines**.
 
• **Blacklisting:** If the **FASTag** account has **insufficient balance**, the tag is blacklisted, and the vehicle owner may be required to pay **double the toll amount** in cash or via electronic modes at the plaza.
</ul

questions.question: Who won the 2025 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction with the novel 'James', a reimagining of 'Huckleberry Finn' from Jim’s perspective?
questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Percival Everett**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Percival Everett** is the recipient of the **2025 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction** for his acclaimed novel **'James'**.
 
• The novel **'James'** serves as a creative and powerful reimagining of **Mark Twain’s** **1884** masterpiece, **'Adventures of Huckleberry Finn'**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the novel's origin is correct.***
 
• The narrative is told entirely from the perspective of **Jim**, the enslaved man who flees with Huck Finn. This shift in viewpoint provides **Jim** with a complex internal life, **intellectual depth**, and a distinct voice that was largely absent in the original text. ***Hence, the statement regarding the perspective of the novel is correct.***
 
• The book explores heavy themes such as **racial identity**, the **hypocrisy of slavery**, and the **subversive power of language** and **literacy** in **19th-century America**.
 
• **'James'** was widely praised by critics for its **satirical edge** and its ability to deconstruct a classic of the **American literary canon** while standing as a significant work of art on its own.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Percival Everett:**
 
 
• He is a highly prolific **American novelist** and a Distinguished Professor of English at the **University of Southern California**.
 
• Born in **1956** in **Georgia**, his work often utilizes **metafiction** and **satire** to critique contemporary **American culture** and **racial politics**.
 
• He is also well-known for his **2001** novel **'Erasure'**, which was later adapted into the **Academy Award-winning** film **'American Fiction'** in **2023**.
 
 
 
• **The Pulitzer Prize for Fiction:**
 
 
• This is one of the seven **Pulitzer Prizes** annually awarded for **Letters, Drama, and Music**.
 
• The award was established in **1917** through the will of **Joseph Pulitzer**, a prominent **newspaper publisher**.
 
• It is administered by **Columbia University** in **New York City** and honors distinguished fiction by an **American author**, preferably dealing with **American life**.
 
 
 
• **The Narrative of 'James':**
 
 
• In Everett's retelling, **Jim** is revealed to be highly **literate** and **articulate**, choosing to speak in a "slave dialect" only as a survival mechanism around white characters.
 
• This **linguistic subversion** is a central feature of the novel, highlighting the **agency** and **intelligence** of those oppressed by **systemic racism**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Literary Impact:** Reimagining classics has become a significant trend in **contemporary literature**, allowing modern authors to fill **historical silences** and provide voices to marginalized characters from **canonical texts**.
 
• **Context of the 2025 Award:** The recognition of **'James'** by the **Pulitzer Board** underscores the ongoing relevance of **American history** and the **Antebellum South** in understanding current **societal structures**.
 
• **Critical Recognition:** Before winning the **Pulitzer Prize**, **'James'** was also a finalist for other major awards like the **National Book Award**, cementing its status as one of the most important books of the **mid-2020s**.
